identity.name: Classique
identity.one_liner: The 39mm Classique perpetual calendar with the fluted caseband and Breguet hands — the dress-watch reference for the oldest name in Swiss watchmaking.

narrative.story: Abraham-Louis Breguet founded the house in 1775, and the Classique line carries the brand's founding design codes: the fluted (coin-edge) caseband, the Breguet hands (the open-tipped "pomme" hands Breguet designed in 1783), and the guilloché dial. The 537/3 caliber is an automatic perpetual calendar based on a Lemania-derived platform with a silicon balance spring. The Classique perpetual is the most-cited Breguet dress complication and the watch a collector cites when they want a perpetual calendar from the house that invented the tourbillon.
narrative.collector_notes: The fluted caseband is hand-knurled. Breguet hands (open-tipped blue steel) are a house signature since 1783. The silicon balance spring is Breguet's modern addition to the classic Lemania base.
